head_commit.message:
ci: stop the linux dependency step hanging for the whole job timeout (#1054)

The release build's apt step had no interactive-prompt suppression, no lock
timeout and no step timeout, so it could block forever. It did: one run sat
in this step from 19:48 to 20:48 until timeout-minutes 60 killed the job,
and every downstream job was skipped with it.

Three separate ways it can block, each closed:

needrestart is apt-hooked on ubuntu-22.04 and prompts for which services to
restart. DEBIAN_FRONTEND does not suppress that one - needrestart reads its
own NEEDRESTART_MODE.

unattended-upgrades holds the dpkg lock and apt waits with no timeout by
default. It is meant to be disabled on hosted images and currently is not:
actions/runner-images#13271 is open, regressed in the 2025-10-23 images and
affects 22.04 and 24.04. DPkg::Lock::Timeout bounds the wait.

debconf can prompt independently, which DEBIAN_FRONTEND covers.

The step timeout is the backstop and matters most on its own: it turns
silently burning the hour and losing the release into failing in 15 with a
log that says which package it died on.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
fix(ats): stop false date-context criticals, and route translation through the active provider (#1051)

* fix(ats): stop a bare present-tense word from faking a date context

is_open_ended matched PRESENT_MARKERS anywhere in a line, so ordinary
prose ("Reduced actual costs by 20% in 2023") read as an open-ended
span and, via factual::unsupported_date_issues' own direct scan of the
same word list, turned a truthful year into a Critical the moment the
source didn't literally spell it out (HIGH: user-facing, blocks ok,
drives the repair loop to rewrite correct content).

Require the marker to sit right after a year (PRESENT_MARKER_ADJACENT_RE)
instead of a bare word search, and route factual.rs's date-context
check through the same structural predicate mod.rs::labels_the_entry_below
already uses (JobEntry or a trailing_date_column) so the two surfaces
can't drift apart again.

Tightening is_open_ended costs bare-marker recognition with no year
anywhere in the fragment ("Present" alone) - accepted, matches the
non-answer DATE_ONLY_MARKERS already gives "Today" alone. It also
silently dropped source_is_ongoing's separator-free coverage
("2021 Present", no dash) - a shape export::parser::DATE_RE itself
accepts - so tenure.rs gets a dedicated SPAN_MARKER_NO_SEP_RE arm to
keep that reading generous rather than closing a truthful long tenure
at its start year (MEDIUM: was reachable, no prior test covered it).

* fix(export): link a bare lowercase domain on an allowlisted tld

A bare portfolio domain with no path (aijobhunter.app, iamsaeed.dev)
rendered as plain text while a GitHub project url one line below, which
happened to carry a /path, rendered as a clickable link. Add a second
bare-domain arm in split_urls gated on lowercase + an explicit TLD
allowlist shared with validate/content/factual.rs's URL_RE, so a
capitalised library name spelled with a dot (Socket.IO, Bun.sh,
Nuxt.dev) still stays plain text and an open-ended TLD class can never
link a node.js-shaped token to an invalid host.

* fix(ats): widen the link guard to the domain the renderer now hyperlinks

BARE_DOMAIN_NO_PATH_RE (model/rich.rs) turns a bare lowercase domain on an
allowlisted TLD into a real hyperlink, but factual.rs's URL_RE couldn't see
that same shape: its bare-host arm needs a known code host, its other
bare-domain arm needs a trailing path. A hallucinated project domain with no
path contributed to neither source_urls nor generated_urls, so
factual.altered_project_link never fired even though the export rendered it
as a real, clickable, seemingly-verified link.

Add a fifth URL_RE arm mirroring the renderer's exact rule (lowercase +
closed TLD allowlist, no path), scoped (?-i:...) against the rest of the
pattern so a capitalised stack-line library name (Socket.IO, Bun.sh,
Nuxt.dev) still stays unmatched. Also correct rich.rs's doc comment, which
claimed its TLD list mirrors URL_RE's bare-host arm when it actually mirrors
the domain+path arm; the real bare-host arm is CODE_HOSTS-gated with a
narrower TLD set.

* fix(ai): translate through the active provider, not the embedding one

Translation read the persisted embedding config as a stand-in for the
active AI provider, so a claude-code user could have a job ad routed to
whatever Ollama chat model embeddings happened to be configured for (an
arbitrary /api/tags-first pick), taking 117s and starving concurrent
embed calls. It now reads ai_config::AiConfigStore::active_config and
always uses the user's own active model, never a pick; the cloud-provider
cost gate is unchanged. Also distinguishes a real Ollama transport timeout
from a connection refusal (both used to read "unreachable") across every
call site in ollama.rs, and logs the embedding model (not just the
provider) on both success and failure, including when the config read
itself falls back to a default.

Embedding routing through the active provider is a separate, out-of-scope
design decision (Claude Code has no embeddings API).

* feat(settings): add prompt quality control to the ai settings page

Canonical home for the global promptQuality preference, previously
changeable only from StepFineTune and AnalyzeLeftPanel — the tailor
pipeline had no control at all. Reads/writes the same store field, so
all three surfaces stay in sync. resolveEffectiveTier ignores the
preference for anything but a local Ollama provider, so the control
stays enabled but names the active provider and states the setting

head_commit.message:
ci: group dependabot updates by area, and unblock local pushes (#1050)

* ci: group dependabot updates by the part of the app they touch

Cargo and github-actions only grouped typst and codeql-action, so every
other bump opened its own PR: 5 Rust crates and 4 workflow actions at once.
npm already had a catch-all and collapsed to a single PR.

Adds the same catch-all to both, named for the area so the PR title says
which part of the app moved (desktop-rust, ci-actions), and renames npm's
group to javascript for the same reason. Majors stay individual on all
three, unchanged.

Both catch-alls carry exclude-patterns for the existing lockstep groups.
exclude-patterns beats patterns, so typst and codeql-action stay in their
own PRs regardless of group order in this file - a partial bump inside a
large catch-all PR would not be visible.

npm stays one entry: workspace members share the root pnpm-lock.yaml and
cannot be split per-directory.

* test: move the vitest browser server off a windows-reserved port

Vitest hardcodes defaultBrowserPort = 63315 and allocates upward from
there. Windows reserves blocks for Hyper-V/WSL in that neighbourhood
(63285-63384 here), and a reserved port is still offered by the resolver
but refused at bind, so every push died on:

  Error: listen EACCES: permission denied ::1:63315

with all 6956 tests passing - vitest counts the unhandled error as a
failure. Reproduced identically three times, sandboxed and not.

Pins browser.api.port to 6317, below the dynamic port range where these
exclusions live. The default was already a fixed port, so this is not
trading a dynamic allocation for a static one - it is the same shape at
an address the OS will actually hand over.

Verified: vitest run --project storybook now serves on localhost:6317,
46 files / 180 tests, exit 0.
